question.text: A client refuses to sell a stock at a loss, hoping it will 'come back'. This is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Disposition effect = tendency to hold losers (refuse to realise loss) and sell winners. Loss-aversion-driven. The Trap: Anchoring is about initial reference; herding is crowd behaviour. Cross-Exam Context: Core behavioural finance. Manager's Pro-Tip: Counter with pre-committed stop-losses — removes discretion at the moment of decision.
